title: Staged canary pipeline for pinned model revisions with safety heuristics and metric-driven routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an engineering pipeline that enables canary rollouts and A/B tests for pinned model revisions with layered safety checks, adaptive traffic heuristics, and automated metric gates. This ticket covers runtime routing logic, gating thresholds, observability hooks, and deterministic fallback policies for pinned variants so product teams can safely validate new model builds in production without broad exposure.
background_context: PM owners requested a safer way to validate pinned model revisions after model onboarding. Current pin behavior swaps revisions atomically and lacks staged verification for safety and performance regressions. This has led to surprises in a few production rollouts. We need an engineerable canary pipeline that integrates with pins and supports multi-variant A/B experiments plus deterministic fallbacks.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Shadow + telemetry collection for 48h on 5% sampled traffic. Phase 2: Safety-filtered canary at 1% traffic for 2 hours, monitor safety and latency signals. Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 10% over 6 hours with automated metric gates. Phase 4: A/B test at 50/50 for targeted workspace cohort for 24h optionally. Phase 5: Full promotion or rollback. All phases support immediate manual abort and automatic fallback to pinned baseline if any gate trips.
gating_and_thresholds: Safety violations (policy classifier false_positive corrected rate) > 0.5% over 1000 examples => fail
Latency p95 increase > 30% relative to baseline over 5m window => fail
Token cost delta > +20% sustained over 1h => alert but do not auto-fail
Semantic quality regression (eval set rolling MRR drop) > 3% => fail
routing_heuristics: Implement edge routing policy that: 1) honors pin scoping (workspace/route), 2) applies canary fraction at request entry, 3) enforces user affinity for A/B cohorts by deterministic hashed user_id, 4) prefers low-latency region variants when available, and 5) supports emergency capacity fallback to lower-cost compatible model variant.
monitoring_and_metrics: sampled hallucination/QA labels via eval hooks
rollback_plan: Immediate fallback to pinned baseline model variant on any auto-fail. For manual rollback, initiate traffic switch with a 60s controlled drain, invalidate KV cache to avoid cross-variant contamination, and emit a change event with correlation id. Postmortem plays: collect sample traces, save failing prompts, schedule hotfix or revert PR.
acceptance_criteria: Engine can apply canary fractions for pinned variants and honor deterministic user affinity
Safety classifier signals are integrated and can trigger automatic rollback
Metrics emitted to console and alerting system within 2 minutes of observation
Automated gates enforce thresholds and log decision reasons in audit trail
Manual abort and emergency fallback succeed without request loss in >99% cases
test_plan: Unit tests for routing logic and deterministic hashing, integration tests simulating mixed traffic with canary fractions, e2e smoke test that executes canary rollout in staging with simulated safety hits, load test for 10% ramp at production QPS, and a small closed beta with two internal teams before wide rollout.
qa_steps: Deploy to staging cluster with pinned baseline and canary flag toggles
Run synthetic prombench load for 2h and verify p95 SLAs
Inject synthetic safety flags and confirm auto-fail path
Validate audit logs include canary decisions and reason codes
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: KV cache cross-contamination between variants. Mitigation: add per-variant cache namespaces and explicit invalidation on rollback.
Risk: Mis-calibrated safety classifier causing false rollbacks. Mitigation: require safety classifier trip plus human-review tag for high-variance routes or use dual-signal gating.
Risk: Increased cost during A/B test. Mitigation: limit cohort size and set cost-alert threshold that notifies PM before exceeding budget.
